newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia dlr struggles feebly to break bonds.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia dlr struggles feebly to break bonds.

text.p: The Australian dollar tested the bounds of its recent tight range Tuesday but the feeble flailing failed to stir the market from its year-end slumber.

The bumpy price action, which had more to do with the patchy market than to meaningful flows, confirmed the resilience of the US$0.7910-0.7950 range which has come to dominate since the currency crumbled from atop 80 cents last week.

The one area of real action was the New Zealand cross where a relatively hawkish monetary policy outlook from the RBNZ put paid to thoughts of further easing there in the short term and sparked a switch by U.S. funds from the A$ to the Kiwi.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the local dollar had bumped up to US$0.7935/40 after dipping to an early US$0.7913/18 low from a US$0.7952 high offshore. It finished Monday at US$0.7930/35.

Dealers said local corporates had been buying in small amounts and there were a lot more bids from US$0.7910 to US$0.7850. However, the repeated failure to crack US$0.7950 was alarming some who saw a real risk of a return to the pivotal US$0.7810 support level if a breakthrough did not come soon.
"I favour it lower," said one at a local bank. "Corporates may have an appetite to buy, but the big U.S. funds are all on the offer and Japanese demand seems to have dried up."
He noted the issuance of yen/A$ dual currency samurai bonds had slowed to a trickle with only two worth a total 60 billion yen launched so far this month.

That could partly be due to simple year-end lethargy, but dealers feared it also reflected the narrowing interest premium offered by A$ assets, particularly after last week's surprise 0.5 point cut in official interest rates to 6.0 percent.

The local dollar certainly suffered in contrast with its Antipodean neighbor today when the RBNZ said a recent market-led easing in New Zealand interest rates had gone too far. The dollar dived to NZ$1.1225/43 in response from NZ$1.1348/36.

The Kiwi dollar shot to US$0.7064/71 from US$0.6985/92 after RBNZ governor Don Brash said the dip in 90-day bank bill rates to around 8.00 percent was overdone and he would prefer 8.5 percent. He also favoured a firm TWI of 66.5 when many had looked for something nearer 65.0.
He said the new wider inflation band of 0-3 percent allowed less scope for easing than might have been assumed and expressed disquiet at some recent data outcomes.
Analysts thought the Kiwi could test 71 cents once offshore markets had absorbed all this and perhaps attract offshore funds which would otherwise have gone to the Australian dollar.
The local dollar also eased to 90.24/34 yen from 90.40/50, but was unchanged in trade weighted terms at 58.9.
There were no economic data out but the government's main commodities agency ABARE released its quarterly outlook for commodity exports in 1996/97.

This confirmed a slowing trend in exports growth with the latest forecast for a 2.5 percent rise to A$58.92 billion against an estimate of A$59.72 billion in the September quarter and A$61.08 billion in Q2.
The only data of note this week will be merchandise imports for November out Wedesday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
